sdidlab fits synthetic difference-in-differences (SDID) for a single treated
unit, with the inference and diagnostics that design needs. This vignette
walks through the whole workflow on the standard example: California's
Proposition 99, which raised the cigarette tax in 1989.

```{r setup}
library(sdidlab)
```

## A panel

sdidlab works on a long data frame, one row per unit and period. You declare
which columns are which with `sdid_panel()`. The Proposition 99 data ship
with synthdid, and `prop99_panel()` wraps them:

```{r}
panel <- prop99_panel()
panel
```

The panel has a 0/1 `treated` column, so sdidlab can work out the treated
unit (California) and the first treated period (1989) by itself. For your own
data, either give `sdid_panel()` a treatment column or put them in the
specification.

## A specification

A specification describes one model completely: outcome, treated unit and
timing, donor pool, covariates, estimator and inference. Anything you leave
out takes its default.

```{r}
spec <- sdid_spec(
  label = "Prop 99, SDID",
  inference = list(replications = 100)
)
spec
```

## Fitting

`fit_spec()` builds the estimator's inputs, fits the model and runs placebo
inference. Placebo standard errors are simulated, so pass a seed to make one
fit reproducible on its own; `seed_for(spec)` derives one from the
specification itself.

```{r}
run <- fit_spec(spec, panel, seed = seed_for(spec))
run
```

The estimate is the published one: Arkhangelsky et al. (2021) report
`r round(run$fit$att, 1)` packs per capita. The point estimate and weights
come straight from `synthdid::synthdid_estimate()`; with no trimming
(`trim_k = Inf`) the standard error is synthdid's own placebo standard error,
draw for draw. The default trims placebos that fit the pre-period more than
five times worse than California does -- see
`vignette("placebo-inference")` for why.

## Looking at the fit

Every plot takes the run and returns a ggplot. The trajectory shows
California against its synthetic control, with the time weights along the
bottom:

```{r}
plot_sdid_trajectory(run)
```

The gap path shows treated minus synthetic in every period, measured against
the baseline SDID subtracts, so its post-period points average to the ATT:

```{r}
plot_gap_path(run)
```

The donor weights show which states make up the synthetic California:

```{r}
plot_donor_weights(run, top_n = 12)
```

And the placebo distribution shows where the standard error came from:

```{r}
plot_placebo_distribution(run)
```

## Comparing specifications

`run_specs()` fits a list of specifications, each with its own seed, and
`sdid_results_table()` collects them. Here the three estimators synthdid
provides, plus a classic synthetic control:

```{r}
specs <- list(
  sdid_spec(label = "SDID", inference = list(replications = 100)),
  sdid_spec(label = "Synthetic control", estimator = "sc", inference = list(replications = 100)),
  sdid_spec(label = "Difference-in-differences", estimator = "did", inference = list(replications = 100))
)
runs <- run_specs(specs, panel, progress = FALSE)
results <- sdid_results_table(runs)
results[, c("label", "ATT", "SE", "ci_lo", "ci_hi", "trend_rmse")]
```

```{r, fig.height = 3}
plot_att_forest(data.frame(label = results$label, att = results$ATT,
                           ci_lo = results$ci_lo, ci_hi = results$ci_hi),
                highlight = "SDID", xlab = "Effect on packs per capita")
```
